title: Connor McDavid
summary:
This document is a comprehensive biographical article about Connor McDavid, the Canadian professional ice hockey centre and captain of the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). The article covers the following main points:

**Introduction and Overview**: The article introduces McDavid as a first overall pick in the 2015 NHL entry draft, widely considered one of the best players of all time, and summarizes his major career achievements, including six Art Ross Trophies, five Ted Lindsay Awards, three Hart Memorial Trophies, and a Conn Smythe Trophy.

**Early Life**: Details McDavid's birth in Richmond Hill, Ontario in 1997, his childhood playing hockey against older children, his time with the York Simcoe Express coached by his father, and his success with the Toronto Marlboros where he won GTHL Player of the Year.

**Playing Career**: 
- *Junior career*: His exceptional player status allowing him to enter the OHL draft at age 15, his tenure with the Erie Otters (2012–2015), where he became the most decorated player in league history and won multiple awards including the Red Tilson Trophy and CHL Player of the Year.
- *Professional career*: Chronologically covering his NHL career with the Oilers, including his injury-shortened rookie season, becoming the youngest captain in NHL history, multiple 100-point seasons, Art Ross and Hart Trophy wins, team struggles from 2017–2020, his historic 2022–23 season with 64 goals and 153 points, the Oilers' 2024 Stanley Cup Final appearance where he won the Conn Smythe Trophy despite losing, and his 2025 contract extension and sixth Art Ross Trophy.

**International Play**: His junior international career with gold medals at the 2013 U18 Championships and 2015 World Juniors, senior career including the 2016 World Championship gold, captaincy of Team North America at the 2016 World Cup, the 4 Nations Face-Off victory, and the 2026 Winter Olympics where he set multiple records and won silver.

**Player Profile**: His reputation among peers and comparisons to Sidney Crosby and Wayne Gretzky, praise for his exceptional skating speed, and criticism of his defensive play.

**Personal Life and Philanthropy**: His marriage to Lauren Kyle, endorsements (NHL 18 cover, BetMGM), and charitable work with Edmonton's Indigenous community.

**Records and Statistics**: Extensive documentation of his career statistics, awards, and numerous NHL, Oilers franchise, and Olympic records.
